name: Claude Code
tagline: Anthropic’s terminal-native coding agent with full-repository context.
verdict: Claude Code is the pick for developers who want an agent that lives in the terminal and composes with real engineering workflows, scripts, CI pipelines, headless automation, rather than a bolted-on chat panel. Its reasoning holds up on genuinely multi-step tasks across a full repository, and it asks permission on sensitive actions instead of working blind. There is no graphical editor, so anyone who wants point-and-click review will feel the gap, and usage-based cost on long autonomous runs is worth watching. It is the strongest option for CI-driven or command-line-first teams, and a weaker fit for developers who want a GUI-first experience. One more factor worth knowing: Claude Code itself passed $1B in run-rate revenue within six months of its public launch, and Anthropic, now backed by a $65B Series H at a $965B valuation, is investing directly in its toolchain, having acquired the Bun JavaScript runtime Claude Code ships as an executable in December 2025. The tradeoff of that single-vendor stack is that Claude Code is tied exclusively to Claude models, with no built-in switch to GPT or Gemini the way some editor-based rivals allow.
